misclassified_entities.reason: Application Layer is typically an internal component of the node stack requesting historical data, not an external entity from outside the system boundary. It represents internal software layers rather than external actors.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote Ethereum node connecting via etha subprotocol. Network peers can send malformed handshakes, falsely advertise data availability, or provide invalid blocks. All data must be validated against protocol rules and cryptographic proofs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Ethereum P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network layer propagating blocks. Network messages can be intercepted, modified, or fabricated by malicious actors. All blocks received must be fully validated including header proofs, transaction signatures, and state roots.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External user or application submitting transactions via JSON-RPC. User inputs are completely untrusted. Transactions must be fully validated including signature verification, nonce checks, balance checks, and gas limits.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Other nodes in the P2P network submitting blocks. Peers may be Byzantine actors attempting to submit invalid blocks or cause consensus failures. All block headers and bodies must be validated cryptographically.

trusted_external_entities.name: Untrusted External Contract
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External contract that may contain malicious code attempting re-entrancy or state modification attacks. This is exactly the threat model STATICCALL addresses - external code is inherently untrusted and must be sandboxed via static context restrictions.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: TCP connection establishment does not imply trust. Handshake validation must verify networkId, genesis hash, and forkId compatibility before accepting peer messages.
All blocks from the network must be fully validated before affecting local state. Includes header validation, transaction validation, and state root verification.
Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce ordering, sufficient balance, gas limit within block limits, and valid transaction encoding.
Block headers from peers require full validation: parent hash linkage, timestamp bounds, gas limit delta constraints, base fee calculation, and proof-of-stake signature verification.
External contracts are untrusted by design. STATICCALL provides sandboxing by preventing state modifications. The STATIC flag must be correctly propagated through all nested calls.
